Start here

You can learn Patch entirely in the browser. Open Patch Studio, edit the source, press Run, and watch the result. The visual Designer edits the same Patch source instead of maintaining a hidden form file.

Fastest path: hosted Patch Studio

  1. Open Patch Studio. The editor and Designer are ready without installing a toolchain.
  2. Replace the sample source with the first program below.
  3. Press Run. Output appears in the result workspace.
  4. Switch to Designer when you start building a Window application.

Offline path

The rolling offline-studio-v0.2 release provides the Stage 1 Offline Studio beta for Windows x64, macOS Apple Silicon and Linux x64. It provides offline authoring, Designer/Object Inspector and Run. Host-native Build directly inside Offline Studio is still the explicit Stage 2 gap.

Your first Patch program

create text message = "Hello, Patch!"
show message

create introduces persistent state. show prints a value. Nothing mutates the state in this example.

Command-line quick start

patch check app.patch
patch run app.patch
patch build app.patch --target web
patch doctor --json

check validates source, run executes supported programs, build creates a selected artifact, and doctor reports compiler/backend health. Machine-readable JSON contracts are available for supported commands.

Build it

Tutorial 1: build a Counter application

  1. Create a number named count. This is the application state.
  2. Create a Window containing a Text control and a Button.
  3. Add a clicked handler for the Button.
  4. Inside the event, mutate count only through an explicit change block.
create number count = 0

window "Counter" size 420, 240:
  text "Count: {count}" at 24, 24 size 220, 32
  button "Add" as add_button at 24, 72 size 120, 38

when add_button clicked:
  change count:
    add 1

The text interpolation {count} reflects the new state after the event. In Patch Studio you can move and resize the controls in Designer and the geometry remains ordinary source.

Open repository exampleTry it in Studio

Tutorial 2: conditions and repeat

Conditions are readable blocks. A literal repeat exposes the current 1-based iteration through count.

create number score = 0

repeat 4:
  if count == 2 or count == 4:
    change score:
      add count

show score

This program adds 2 and 4, then shows 6. The persistent mutation remains visible even when it is nested inside control flow.

Open repository exampleSimpler if/else example

Tutorial 3: Things, recipes and bounded authority

A Thing groups named fields. A recipe can be paired with an allow declaration that restricts which semantic effects are permitted.

create thing player:
  name = "Mia"
  score = 0

allow reward:
  player.score may increase up to 10

make reward(player):
  change player:
    add 5 to score

do reward(player)
show player.score

The recipe requests an increase of 5 and the declared capability permits an increase up to 10. Patch can reason about the semantic direction and, where provable, its magnitude.

Open repository example

Tutorial 4: data controls and transient selection

GUI selection is not automatically persistent state. A changed handler receives transient value, and persistence happens only when the handler performs a Patch change.

create list fruits = ["Banana", "Mango"]

window "Fruit Picker":
  listbox "Apple", "Banana", "Cherry", "Mango" as fruits

when fruits changed:
  change fruits:
    set = value

Because fruits is list state, the ListBox uses multi-selection on supported targets and value is a transient text list.

Language guide

Values and state

Current product state includes number, text, boolean, list and Thing values. Things are finite own-field records with prototype-meta names rejected.

Explicit change

Persistent mutation is expressed inside change. Common semantic operations include set, add, remove and clear according to the target type.

Control flow

if/else and repeat structure execution while keeping nested mutation explicit.

Recipes

make declares reusable behavior and do calls it. Range-bounded parameters and capability checks are supported in the current language subset.

GUI applications and Patch Studio

Patch Studio is a source-backed RAD environment. The editor, Designer, Object Inspector, Project Tree, Resource Manager and component tools operate on the same project source. There is no separate hidden persistent form model.

Typical visual workflow

  1. Create or select a Form from the Form selector.
  2. Add a control from the searchable Component Palette.
  3. Move or resize it in Designer, or edit geometry directly in source.
  4. Use Object Inspector for source-backed properties and Events.
  5. Press Run to compile and execute the current project.
  6. Use Build only for a target that the capability matrix reports as supported.

Current component families

Patch includes source-backed Forms and current authoring/runtime paths for Text, Button, Input, Checkbox, Radio, ComboBox, ListBox, Table, TreeView, Tabs, Slider, Panel, Menu, dialogs, Picture, Shape, PaintBox, Timer, StatusBar and ImageList metadata. Target parity is explicit and conservative.

Open the generated component capability matrix

Forms and multi-window applications

Named Forms can be opened and closed through Patch application behavior. The Designer materializes only the active Form's controls while preserving source-backed shells for the other Forms. Runtime events now reconcile keyed Forms so unchanged Form DOM can remain stable.

Designer performance model

The primary Designer preview uses a declaration-only design snapshot instead of executing application behavior. Large projects use active-Form materialization. Current runtime rendering uses stable keyed Form/control identities, preserves bounded transient browser state around changed-Form replacement, and updates Tabs locally rather than rebuilding every Form.

Run, build and distribute

Patch exposes different output paths rather than pretending every backend has identical capabilities.

GoalRecommended pathNotes
Learn and prototypeHosted Patch StudioFastest visual edit/run loop.
Work without internetOffline Studio Stage 1Offline authoring, Designer/Object Inspector and Run.
Standalone web apppatch build app.patch --target webProduces supported standalone Web output.
Local supported desktop artifactReady/offline compiler pathCurrent Windows/macOS/Linux Window contract is Native GUI IR 1.7 / payload v17 / runtime v1.8.
Portable numeric backendC99 / direct Wasm where supportedThese subsets fail closed on unsupported language features.

Signing status matters: Windows Offline Studio is currently unsigned by Authenticode, Linux is unsigned, and macOS uses ad-hoc signing only. Production Developer ID/notarization and Windows signing remain explicit open release work.

Native and release contracts

Patch intentionally keeps two live native product contracts: the current Native GUI IR 1.7 / payload v17 / runtime v1.8 facade and the IR 1.2 / payload v12 / runtime v1.3 frozen TreeView compatibility line. Newer features never silently reinterpret the frozen contract.
